clue.text: Breaking news: trouble — boss number 5 sacked (hammer replacement)

indicators.note: the Roman numeral for five is fired from the word just before it, so that letter goes

parts.note: N is a standard abbreviation for news
to ail is to trouble or afflict
guv, short for guv'nor, is British slang for the boss
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A news flash about a troublesome boss, number five on some list, being given the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: GUV loses its V (5 in Roman numerals) to leave GU, giving N + AIL + GU + N = NAIL GUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail gun drives nails mechanically, doing the job a hand-held tool for knocking in nails used to do.

clue.text: All but one mounted horse

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so the letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: 'all but one' is 'all bar one', so but here means bar, except
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Every horse but one has a rider on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but one' reads as 'bar a', which turns upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab is a famous breed of horse from the Arabian peninsula, prized for stamina and its dished face.

clue.text: Dirty looks when Henry resigns over topical film

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means turned upside down, so the whole string is read upward
Henry stands for its symbol, and resigning means it leaves the word next to it

parts.note: leers are lecherous or sly looks
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets filthy glares as a man named Henry steps down from his post.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance; WHEN without it is WEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short film of current events shown in cinemas before television news.

clue.text: Take some exercise, fool!

parts.note: to do a class or course is to take it
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone is told off as a fool and ordered to go and get some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is informal for a stupid person, an idiot or dimwit.

clue.text: Referring to help for poor areas

parts.note: re means regarding or about
alms are charitable gifts for the needy

explanation.surface: A memo about aid for deprived parts of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are domains or fields, spheres of activity or territory.

clue.text: Change to diagonal a pain

indicators.note: an order to change these words means their letters are rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that switching something to a diagonal layout is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pain' sounds like slang for a nuisance, but here it is the definition proper: a medical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Odontalgia is the medical term for toothache, a specific kind of ache in the mouth.

clue.text: Flier's down — fool!

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling down
tit is British slang for an idiot

explanation.surface: Someone calls a pilot a gloomy idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier's down' suggests a plane coming down or a bird's feathers; down is the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue tit is a small European garden bird, and birds are fliers.

clue.text: Some say run Grand National here

indicators.note: only some of the next words' letters are used, a run that spans them

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: People say the big steeplechase is held at this racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr racecourse, in south-west Scotland, stages the Scottish Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish version of the famous steeplechase is staged each April at the racecourse in this Ayrshire town.

clue.text: Undermine what 'orseman did

indicators.note: the apostrophe shows a dropped aitch, so the phrase is said the same careless way

parts.note: a horseman: he rode

explanation.surface: A cockney rider is accused of sabotage.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with a dropped H, as the 'orseman would, 'he rode' becomes 'e rode.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, weakening the base of something, as water undermines a cliff.

clue.text: Who had a 17, 21, 1 in store?

parts.note: Del Boy of the sitcom Only Fools and Horses famously fell through the bar flap in a wine bar
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A quiz question: who was in for a nasty tumble?
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references give FALL THROUGH THE BAR, Del Boy's most famous scene; Only Fools and Horses is a classic BBC sitcom about South London market traders.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Unprepared — is daughter going to make excuses?

indicators.note: the daughter going means her abbreviation leaves the preceding word

parts.note: ad lib means improvised, without preparation
taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent wonders whether their unready daughter will start making excuses.
explanation.walkthrough: The daughter looks like the person making excuses, but she only supplies the letter that must leave the improvised phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Alibis are claims of being elsewhere, and loosely any excuses offered to escape blame.

clue.text: General attacked north German town

indicators.note: something attacked is knocked about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A wartime report of a general launching an assault on a town in the north of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places the town in the north, but Erlangen is in Bavaria; north just supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Erlangen is a university city in Bavaria, near Nuremberg, home of Siemens' medical business.

clue.text: Man U get beaten by Spurs at last! They will make changes

indicators.note: a beaten team is battered about, so its letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of the club name

explanation.surface: A football headline: Manchester United are finally beaten by Tottenham, prompting a shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Man U is Manchester United; Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur. 'They will make changes' sounds like a manager rotating the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutagens are agents such as radiation or chemicals that alter an organism's DNA.

clue.text: Army chief, ennobled like Newton, ruined? Nothing in it

indicators.note: in it tells us to put the nought inside the word just before

parts.note: a la means in the style of
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
broke means bankrupt, financially ruined
O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: A general raised to the peerage like Isaac Newton, then disgraced with nothing left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like Newton' suggests Sir Isaac, but Newton is the unit of force. Alan Brooke was made Viscount Alanbrooke.
explanation.definitionFit: Field Marshal Alan Brooke, Chief of the Imperial General Staff in WWII, was created Viscount Alanbrooke.

clue.text: Pretend to keep old place in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: sham means fake or pretend
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone fakes keeping an old house in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Soham is a small fenland town in East Cambridgeshire, between Ely and Newmarket.

clue.text: So full of crap still

indicators.note: full of means holding something inside, so one word is stuffed into the other

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, so
tat is cheap, worthless junk

explanation.surface: Someone complains: so full of rubbish, still.
explanation.walkthrough: Tat is British slang for tawdry rubbish. SIC appears in quotations to mark text reproduced as found.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means motionless or unchanging, not moving at all.

clue.text: Not happen after some months in Hollywood discussing cast

parts.note: Americans call autumn fall

indicators.note: discussing means talking about, so the word is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: to cast is to throw; past tense threw

explanation.surface: A deal collapses in Hollywood after months of talks about who is in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a film's actors in a Hollywood surface; here it is the verb, past of throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall through is an idiom for a plan or deal failing to come off.

clue.text: Cannon, maybe, or canon? One needs deleting

indicators.note: the instruction says the letter for one must be struck out

parts.note: a canon is a church law or decree
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spelling query: is it cannon or canon? One of them has a letter too many.
explanation.walkthrough: ORDINANCE (a decree) minus I gives the military word; the spelling joke mirrors cannon versus canon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means artillery and military supplies, and a cannon is an example of heavy artillery.

clue.text: What it costs to run horse

parts.note: a charge is a price or fee
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone asks the price of keeping a horse to race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to run horse' suggests racing costs; to run is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a war horse, a mount trained for cavalry charges.

clue.text: Make OFAH situation extremely funny — one's captivated

indicators.note: captivated suggests being held captive inside something else
something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Write an Only Fools and Horses scenario that is extremely funny and holds the audience captive.
explanation.walkthrough: OFAH is fans' shorthand for Only Fools and Horses, the theme sitcom; 'situation' nods to sitcom too.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to shape or make it, especially by hand.

clue.text: Illness partly stopping judge — he may be one of them

definitions.text: he may be one of them

indicators.note: only part of the second word plugs a gap in the first, the rest trailing after

parts.note: TB is tuberculosis
a judge hears a case

explanation.surface: A judge is laid low by illness; perhaps he is one of the stricken.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion is unusual: only the first half of the judge's verb sits inside the disease, the rest trailing behind. The definition points back to the judge, who comes from the barristers' profession.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar is the legal profession of barristers, so a lawyer or judge may be a member of it.

clue.text: Sport initially on Sky beginning to irritate Irishman

parts.note: RU are the initials of rugby union
the air is the sky

indicators.note: initially points to initials, the first letters of a sport's name
the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Sport on Sky TV starts to annoy an Irish viewer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky looks like the British satellite broadcaster beside Sport; it is the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruairi is an Irish male given name, the Gaelic form of Rory.

clue.text: School in Chennai that's good

parts.note: Madras is the former name of Chennai
ah is an exclamation of satisfaction

explanation.surface: Praise for a school in the Indian city of Chennai.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrasah is an Islamic school or college for religious instruction.

clue.text: Superior skill overcomes Josh's predecessor

indicators.note: to overcome is to come over and around something, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: art is skill or craft
the curry rogan josh: this word comes before josh

explanation.surface: A gifted player outdoes the person who held the post before Josh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Josh's predecessor' sounds like whoever held a job before a man called Josh; it is the word before josh in the curry rogan josh.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior in the sense of haughty, looking down on others, is what arrogant means.

clue.text: High score — 80 percent

indicators.note: keeping eighty percent of a five-letter word keeps four, so the last fifth goes

parts.note: a tally is a score or count

explanation.surface: A scorer boasts of a high score, eighty percent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall and high both describe something of great height.

clue.text: Christie's originally gave auctioneer table — I've got it outside

indicators.note: outside says the exclamation is wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: aha is the cry of sudden understanding

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the first letter of each word

parts.note: the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: At Christie's, the auction house, an auctioneer hands over a table and the buyer exclaims in triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: Christie's looks like the auction house, but the 's means 'is' and Christie is the crime writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was the English crime novelist who created Poirot and Miss Marple.

clue.text: Gave good service to one department

parts.note: the ace is the one in a pack of cards
D is an abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: Someone provided excellent service to a single department of a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests office work; it is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, to ace an opponent is to serve a ball they cannot touch.

clue.text: Fool hit kerb

indicators.note: something hit is knocked out of shape, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An idiot driver bumps into the edge of the pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerb is the British spelling of curb, the pavement edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Berk is mild British slang for a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: One remains responsible for relative in van

indicators.note: in the van means in the lead, so this part is placed at the front

parts.note: rel is a short form of relative
i/c stands for in charge

explanation.surface: One person stays behind to look after a relative riding in a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' suggests a vehicle, but in the van means at the front, as in vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is one of the things that survive from the past, an object left over.

clue.text: Green author

definitions.meaning: first meaning: environmentally friendly, as a prefix
second meaning: Umberto, Italian novelist of The Name of the Rose

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a novelist who is new or naive; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix means environmental, and Umberto of that surname wrote The Name of the Rose.
